message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait/EFO and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (abdominal aortic aneurysm; one is prevalent AAA). Prefer disease-focused, multi-cohort development over pan-trait/framework scores when endpoint fidelity is comparable. PGS003972 (PRS-CS; Nat Genet 2023 AAA GWAS meta-analysis) is the most clearly disease-focused, multi-cohort candidate with a direct AAA endpoint and broad external cohort context (many contributing cohorts listed), and its reported full-model AUROC=0.69 is broadly consistent with other AAA candidates, without relying on obviously heavy/biomarker covariates (covariates are listed as Unknown, which limits comparability but does not indicate leakage). Main limitation: performance reporting is mostly full-model (not explicitly PGS-only) and covariates are unknown; additionally PGS003973 from the same publication reports a much higher C-index (0.882) but with a different covariate set and metric type, making cross-candidate comparability unclear—so confidence is moderated rather than high."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (abdominal aortic aneurysm), so selection hinges on comparably interpretable performance plus study/validation support. PGS003972 is preferred because it comes from a clearly disease-focused AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet; many contributing cohorts listed) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with EUR evaluation, which domain guidance suggests should generally outrank pan-trait/framework or portability-sweep scores when endpoints are similarly aligned. However, the evidence remains insufficient for a high-quality direct pick because reported discrimination is not PRS-comparable across candidates: several models report only full-model AUROC/C-index (e.g., PGS003972 AUROC=0.69; PGS003973 C-index=0.882; PGS001784 full_model AUROC=0.868) or partial-r (PGS002054) without incremental/PGS-only AUROC, and covariates are unknown for some (PGS003972/PGS003429), making the high C-index/AUROC figures potentially covariate-driven and not directly rankable. The strongest PRS-isolated metric shown is PGS001784 PGS-only R2=0.014661 (EUR eval, n=350,767) but it is from a global biobank framework paper, and its advantage is mainly metric availability rather than a disease-focused evidence package. Given these comparability gaps and missing covariate clarity, confidence is low and the overall outcome is sub-optimal despite direct matches being present."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (abdominal aortic aneurysm; one is explicitly prevalent AAA). {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping strings (mostly 'Abdominal aortic aneurysm'; one 'Prevalent abdominal aortic aneurysm'). However, confidence is limited because most candidates lack clearly PRS-only AUROC/incremental metrics, one framework model (PGS001784) reports a very high full-model AUROC (0.868) that is not directly comparable to PRS-only performance, and the heritability sanity-check guidance cautions against over-interpreting covariate-boosted full-model discrimination."}
